title: Quarterly Renewal & Geo Growth Touchpoint
next_steps: Send revised renewal quote with EU region add-on and burst pricing (Maya) - due 2025-10-13
Schedule Private/VPC pilot kickoff: propose dates (Liam) - due 2025-10-15
Run 48-hour latency/cost benchmark on dedicated fleet with customer prompt set (Samira/Liam) - target start 2025-10-20
Share SOC 2 + KMS integration docs and audit log examples (Maya) - due 2025-10-10
action_items: Maya: update quote to include 3k reserved tokens/month baseline + EU geocluster add-on; include burst pricing; due 2025-10-13
Liam: prepare private deployment runbook and checklist for VPC + KMS; include network diagrams; due 2025-10-15
Samira: hand over representative prompt set and traffic profile for benchmarking; due 2025-10-14

summary: Quarterly renewal touchpoint focused on agreement extension and capacity bump from baseline to cover expected growth. Customer wants EU region turned up for data residency and an APAC private pilot evaluation. Main concerns: KMS/integration, audit logs, latency SLAs, and cost tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated vs private. Agreed next steps include revised quote, pilot planning, and benchmarks.
topics: renewal terms, capacity uplift, EU region onboarding, private/VPC pilot, KMS/SOC2/compliance, latency vs cost tradeoffs, rollout strategy
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, we wanted to do a quick quarterly renewal + growth touchpoint. We have about 55 minutes on the invite so feel free to jump in.
[00:18] Priya Kaur: Hi Maya, hi Liam. Thanks, we want to walk through the renewal numbers and our ops constraints — we've got a board motion to lock into a new vendor footprint for EU residency in Q4 so timing is tight.
[00:31] Liam O'Neill: Got it, and congrats on the board motion — that helps clarify timeline. Quick question before we jump in, is the ask mainly data residency or also lower p99 latency for EU traffic?
[00:43] Evan Brooks: Both. Residency is mandatory, p99 under 220ms for inference ideally. Right now some of our EU traffic is routed from US and that isn't acceptable.
[00:55] Samira Patel: Also we have a new recommendation engine ramp next month that will increase token volume ~2.5x. So we need capacity planning and fallback strategies.
[01:08] Maya Chen: Thank you — so from what I heard: capacity uplift for ramp, EU region onboarding and an APAC pilot for latency. Anything on compliance?
[01:18] Priya Kaur: SOC 2 evidence and how you handle KMS/HSM keys — we need to show auditors the end-to-end flow. Also audit logs retention for 13 months.
[01:30] Liam O'Neill: Noted. For KMS we support customer-managed keys in dedicated and private deployments, and HSM-backed options for our private build. I can share the integration doc.
[01:42] Jordan Lee: Quick procurement note — we prefer a 12-month extension with a 30 day cancellation window during the pilot phase. Can that be accommodated?
[01:51] Maya Chen: We can be flexible — I'll include a 30-day pilot cancellation clause in the quote for the EU add-on and private pilot line items.
[02:00] Evan Brooks: On capacity: what's the typical throughput per GPU on your dedicated fleet for the model we run? We saw variability in the benchmark spreadsheet from last year.
[02:12] Liam O'Neill: For the Llama-variant you run, steady-state throughput per GPU is about X tokens/sec under our continuous batching; variability depends on sequence length and KV cache hit rate. We can run a 48-hour benchmark with your prompt set to give concrete numbers.
[02:29] Samira Patel: That would be ideal — our prompts are long (avg 1,100 tokens) so batching behavior is important.
[02:38] Priya Kaur: A question on private vs dedicated — dedicated is appealing for predictability and cost, private is for residency and full network control. Can you describe the gap in operational effort?
[02:51] Liam O'Neill: Sure. Dedicated is a managed tenant in our infra — minimal ops on your side, we handle upgrades, autoscaling policies; Private (VPC) requires more initial setup — networking, peering, KMS config — but we provide a deployment runbook and our SREs work with your netops. For air-gapped on-prem we do an appliance-style install which is more involved.
[03:09] Evan Brooks: And patching/rollouts for private — do you handle canary model rollouts?
[03:16] Liam O'Neill: Yes, we provision a private control plane for rollouts; you can choose canary percentages and automatic fallback. We also expose tracing hooks for end-to-end latency measurement.
[03:26] Maya Chen: On pricing, the ask from Samira was ~2.5x token growth. We discussed a baseline reserved capacity with burst buffer. I will propose a 3k baseline with a defined burst pool.
[03:38] Priya Kaur: What's the SLA delta if we add EU geocluster vs keep hosted? Are SLAs stronger for dedicated?
[03:46] Liam O'Neill: SLAs are stronger on Dedicated with credits for sustained breaches. Hosted has a standard SLA for availability but Dedicated and Private can get tighter targets, we can enumerate in the contract.
[03:56] Samira Patel: For the APAC pilot, we want to try a private node footprint in Singapore for a 6-week window. Is there a minimum commitment?
[04:07] Maya Chen: For pilots we usually have a short-term pilot addendum with scaled down commitment; we can structure a 6-week pilot with a pilot fee and option to convert to a full commitment.
[04:18] Evan Brooks: Network-wise, we need predictable egress IPs for our allowlist and peering details. Liam, can you include example network diagrams and firewall rules?
[04:28] Liam O'Neill: Absolutely — I'll include a sample VPC layout and IP space.
[04:33] Jordan Lee: On procurement timing — if we sign by end of October, can you guarantee EU geocluster available by mid-November?
[04:42] Maya Chen: We'll aim for mid-November but will make availability contingent on capacity lead times. I'll coordinate with infra planning once quote is accepted.
[04:50] Priya Kaur: Another question — how are logs handled for privacy? We need to ensure PII is redacted and that logs stored in EU don't leave the region.
[04:59] Liam O'Neill: We have region-scoped audit log storage and configurable retention. For PII redaction we recommend application-side tokenization, but we also have a built-in option to mask outputs. I'll include details.
[05:12] Samira Patel: For benchmarks, can we measure cost per 1k tokens at p95 latency targets? We want cost sensitivity under different batching and quantization profiles.
[05:22] Liam O'Neill: Yes — the Optimize team runs quantization scenarios; I'll run three profiles: high-quality (no quant), balanced (q8/q4), and low-cost quantized. We'll report cost/token and latency distributions.
[05:34] Maya Chen: Great. To recap — action items, I'll send updated quote with the pilot clause and EU add-on by Oct 13, Liam will prepare private runbook and diagrams by Oct 15, Samira will provide prompt sets by Oct 14, Evan to confirm netops contact by Oct 10. We'll schedule the pilot kickoff after the quote is accepted.
[05:52] Priya Kaur: That works. Thanks everyone.
[05:55] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email with links to the docs and the timeline.

NOTES: occasional transcription artifacts: 'geocluster' sometimes transcribed as 'geo cluster', 'KMS' sometimes 'KMSs'. Names occasionally partial. References to 'X tokens/sec' left intentionally generic where benchmarks pending. Links referenced: security packet (link sent after call), pilot runbook (to be attached), revised quote (to be sent).
